# Human Knowledge: Its Scope and Limits

*[Russell](../philosophers/russell.md) · 1948*

His last large work of epistemology. Russell argues that scientific inference can be justified only by admitting postulates about the structure of the world which experience does not prove, and that what it yields is never certainty but a degree of credibility. The book closes on the admission that all human knowledge is uncertain, inexact and partial.
